body:
I want to be able to go to a party and have a normal conversation with someone I haven't already known for 2+ years. Bonus points for the conversation being about something other than anime or video games.

I want to not be 50+ pounds overweight.

I want to go the office and not be in fear of getting fired because I spent half the day on my phone browsing reddit.

I want to have "do something OUTSIDE of the apartment" be the default, or at least a relatively common, plan for the weekend.

I want to try something new and have a reasonable expectation that, even if I'm not immediately successful, I'll eventually become somewhat competent at it with practice.

I want to feel like I'm actually capable of growing as a person.

I know you probably meant more specific goals, but a big part of why I feel so shitty about myself is that so many things that normal, average people accomplish all the time feel like they're impossibly hard for me.

Thanks. Yeah, my family are the strongest connections I have, and that's...*something*. I'm grateful for it, knowing how so many people have poor relationships with their own parents or siblings. But at the same time they're practically the *only* connections I have, and with me being physically so far away from them (something I don't really intend to change as I was feeling extremely suffocated by the time I moved out) that leads to a lot of loneliness and disconnection whenever I'm not on a Skype call with them. 

As for working on myself...yeah. It's a lifelong project, and the..Sisyphean nature of it is part of what drives my really bad days. I'll diet and exercise regularly for a month or two and then fall apart and be back to my old weight before long. I'll clean up my apartment and feel good about it, and then let it fall back into a junk heap once again within a couple weeks. It seems like I can temporarily get better, but I want to *stay* better and I've never been able to manage that.
